title: Knowledge check: Advantages and Limitations of Express.js

questions.prompt: In Advantages and Limitations of Express.js, which statement best describes Minimalist and flexible architecture?
options: Middleware runs in registered order. Each function must end the response, call next() to continue, or forward an error; avoid accidentally doing more than one of these.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Trace the request from client through middleware and route/service logic to its response. Keep HTTP concerns separate from business rules and data access.
questions.answer_key: Trace the request from client through middleware and route/service logic to its response. Keep HTTP concerns separate from business rules and data access.
questions.explanation: Trace the request from client through middleware and route/service logic to its response. Keep HTTP concerns separate from business rules and data access.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Advantages and Limitations of Express.js?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
questions.answer_key: Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.
questions.explanation: Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.

questions.prompt: A change related to Advantages and Limitations of Express.js appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
